bindings.label: Patient experienced chest pain and shortness of breath for 2 months
32-year-old male with no cough, expectoration, or hemoptysis; no limb swelling or lump; no abdominal pain or weight loss; no history of tobacco smoking or other addictions
Vital signs: pulse rate 92 beats per minute, respiratory rate 20 per minute, blood pressure 116/78 mmHg, oxygen saturation 95%
Chest examination showed a dull note on percussion and absent breath sounds in the entire right hemithorax, except for normal breath sounds in the right infraclavicular area
Chest radiograph revealed a large, nonhomogeneous opacity in the right hemithorax, denser in the middle and lower lung zones, with mild displacement of the mediastinum toward the left

Ultrasonography identified a large, heterogeneous, hypoechoic mass lesion in the right hemithorax with intratumoral vessels on Doppler; abdominal ultrasonography showed no evidence of abdominal mass or metastasis
CECT shows a 20.8×13.6×13 cm heterogeneous right hemithoracic mass with fat/calcification, pleural base, 10 HU, and compressive atelectasis without invasion
Biopsy reveals myxoid tissue, atypical cells, lipoblasts, S100 positivity, and Alcian blue-positive mucin
Pathologist and radiologist expert analyses concur that the right hemithoracic mass is neoplastic and favor myxoid liposarcoma
FUS-DDIT3 and MDM2/CDK4 molecular testing, PET/MRI, and LDH results are unavailable, leaving subtype, grade, and staging unconfirmed
